pull.title: kernel: prevent dangling iterators from temporary ranges
pull.body:
**Problem:** Kernel wrapper methods return `Range` views by value, but their iterators point to the `Range` object.
Saving an iterator from a temporary view, such as `block.Transactions().begin()`, leaves it pointing to the destroyed view, so later use has undefined behavior.

**Fix:** Make range iterators point to the underlying Kernel wrapper object and use the range's compile-time getter for element access.
Remove `operator->`, which returned elements by value and could not easily support arrow expressions.

Point them to the underlying container, use the range's getter for element access, and remove `operator->`, which returned elements by value and could not support arrow expressions.

comments.body:
`operator->` is not implemented correctly. Not your fault; it was broken before. But since you touch that code, you might want to fix it and cover it in a test.

For `operator->` to work correctly, it has to return something that provides `operator->` itself. If `operator*` returns an rvalue, you may need an [arrow_proxy](https://quuxplusone.github.io/blog/2019/02/06/arrow-proxy/).

Good catch, I ended up removing `operator->` instead of adding an arrow proxy, the [standard specification for `transform_view::iterator`](https://eel.is/c++draft/range.transform.iterator) likewise provides `operator*` without `operator->`.
Added you as a co-author.

nit: `value_type` can also be deduced I suppose and removed from template parameter?

```cpp
using value_type = std::invoke_result_t<decltype(GetFunc), const Collection&, size_t>;
```
